# Open-source licences

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_licenses.py from docs/third-party.json. Do not edit this file: edit the JSON and run the script. -->

VaultInk's own code is under the MIT licence (see [LICENSE](../LICENSE)). The firmware binaries also contain wolfSSL (GPL-2.0-or-later) and libraries under the Apache-2.0 licence (NimBLE-Arduino, JPEGDEC, PNGdec, AnimatedGIF, ESP-IDF). The Apache-2.0 licence is compatible with version 3 of the GPL but not with version 2, so the binaries are distributed under the terms of the GPL-3.0-or-later, with the source in this repository. Every other library, font and icon keeps its own licence, and that licence applies to it. They are all listed below.

## What that means for you

- You may use VaultInk, study how it works, change it and share it.
- If you share the firmware binary, changed or not, you must also offer its source code under the same terms. The source is this repository: <https://github.com/Somnius/VaultInk>.
- If you reuse one library from the list, follow that library's licence.
- This page is not legal advice.

## How this list is checked

Each licence below was read from the library's own licence file, source header or package metadata; the last column names the file. Where no such file could be read, the licence says `not verified` instead of a guess. Paths that start with `.pio/`, `~/.platformio/` or `~/.gradle/` are the copies the build tools download; `freeink-sdk/` is a git submodule. The same list is on the device (Settings > System > About > Open-source licences), in [NOTICE](../NOTICE) and in the companion app's About screen.

Notes:

- **wolfSSL**: Dual-licensed: GPL or a commercial licence from wolfSSL Inc. VaultInk uses it under the GPL. Its library.json says GPL-2.0-only; the LICENSING file and the source headers say version 2 or any later version. Source headers say version 2 or later, so it can be combined under GPL version 3, which the Apache-2.0 code in the binary needs.
- **FreeType**: Portions of this software are copyright (c) The FreeType Project (www.freetype.org). All rights reserved. FreeType's LICENSE.TXT offers the FreeType License or the GPL version 2 (or later) and says the FreeType License is compatible with GPL version 3 but not version 2. The firmware binary is distributed under GPL-3.0-or-later, so FreeType is used under the FreeType License, which is compatible with GPL version 3 (not with version 2).
- **ESP-IDF**: ESP-IDF bundles further components (FreeRTOS, lwIP, mbedTLS, newlib and others) under their own licences. Those were not checked one by one.
- **NimBLE-Arduino**: Its NOTICE also credits esp32-snippets, Copyright 2017 Neil Kolban.
- **WebSockets**: Its library.json says LGPL-2.1; the source headers say version 2.1 or any later version.
- **miniz**: The first lines of miniz.h also point to an Unlicense (public domain) statement, which is in miniz.c. The FreeInk SDK's copy of miniz has a LICENSE file with the same MIT text.
- **minibidi (from mintty)**: The licence is named in the header comments of the port; the original licence text is not in this repository.
- **Lucide icons**: No licence file to read: the SDK's lucide submodule is not checked out. A comment in src/components/icons/customListIcons.h says ISC; the FreeInk SDK README says MIT.
- **Hyphenation patterns (typst/hypher)**: The pattern files are downloaded by scripts/update_hyphenation.sh and stored as generated tables; no licence file comes with them. The polytonic Greek patterns were built from tex-hyphen's hyph-el-polyton.tex.
- **HTML entity table (diy-esp32-epub-reader)**: lib/Epub/Epub/htmlEntities.cpp says it is based on this project; its licence file is not in this repository.
- **Self-hosted LiveSync (document id scheme)**: lib/LiveSync/LiveSyncIds.h says the id scheme is ported from the plugin; the plugin's licence file is not in this repository. VaultInk is not affiliated with the project.

## Not in this list

- Tools that only run on the developer's computer and are not in any binary: GoogleTest (host tests), SDL2 (the simulator), Python and its packages (build scripts).
- The libraries that the companion app's libraries pull in themselves (other AndroidX modules), apart from Okio.
- The components inside ESP-IDF, as its note says.
